intro: Computer Science and Engineering student at UC Merced, focused on security and systems programming.

Most of what I build sits below the application layer: runtime patching against a Unity IL2CPP target, an asset compiler that recovers geometry and task graphs out of decompiled prefabs, cross-platform install tooling. I'm drawn to the gap between how a system is documented and how it actually behaves, which is the same thing that pulled me toward security.

work.name: super-squad-among-us
work.desc: Client-side runtime addon for a Unity IL2CPP game. Harmony patching, reflection-driven registration with no manual wiring, and release channels derived entirely from the version string.

work.name: skeld-to-li
work.desc: Asset pipeline that reads a decompiled Unity prefab and recompiles its geometry, colliders and task graph into a third-party map format.

work.name: canvas-to-discord
work.desc: Two scheduled GitHub Actions mirroring an LMS into Discord. HTML-to-markdown conversion so formatting survives, independent state per bot, configured entirely through repository secrets.

work.name: 67-Race
work.desc: Full-stack multiplayer racing game. Flask API with JWT auth and bcrypt-hashed credentials behind a vanilla JS client.

work.name: among-us-mod-updater
work.desc: POSIX install-and-update script targeting Linux, macOS and Windows through WSL, with no runtime dependencies beyond a shell.

work.name: SpectralAnalyzer
work.desc: Real-time spectral analysis of audio input.
